title: Using All the Exponent Rules
short: Simplify expressions with several rules at once.
trouble: Students apply a rule meant for multiplication to addition, writing x² + x³ = x⁵.

blocks.html: You now have five exponent rules. Each one comes from counting factors, so you can always check a rule with small numbers when you are unsure. This lesson puts them together.

Every rule is about multiplying, because an exponent is shorthand for repeated multiplication. None of them says anything about adding. $x^{2} + x^{3}$ adds two different kinds of things, like 2 apples plus 3 oranges, so it stays as it is.
Simplify one step at a time, from the inside out: powers of powers first, then products, then quotients. Give the final answer with positive exponents.

blocks.title: Two letters and a negative exponent
steps: Put it together with positive exponents: $\dfrac{3b^{4}}{a^{5}}$.

blocks.html: Using a multiplication rule on a sum: $x^{2} + x^{3} = x^{5}$. Check with $x = 2$: $4 + 8 = 12$, but $2^{5} = 32$. Only like terms combine when you add, and then the exponent stays put: $3x^{2} + 4x^{2} = 7x^{2}$.
